If I could make one change to iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, it would be to disable the newly added ability to summon Siri AI with a downward swipe gesture. There are already enough ways to invoke Siri without adding another gesture that breaks my habit of opening Notification Center.

On the Mac side, macOS 27 Golden Gate is almost entirely good news. Even as late August, the new beta versions keep delivering delightful surprises. Still, before macOS 27 ships next month, there is one change I am still hoping to see.

macOS 27 Golden Gate makes MacBook battery percentage harder to read

macOS 27 Golden Gate has redesigned the menu bar battery control. By default, the percentage is not shown at all — just a visual battery shape indicator.

It looks clean enough. I do the same thing on my iPhone, turning off the percentage and using the same battery icon. But on the Mac I have always preferred to show the percentage.

If you turn on the "Show Percentage" option in macOS 27 Golden Gate, the number goes inside the battery icon. I assume this is for consistency with how the iPhone does it in iOS 27.

Putting the percentage inside the battery icon is Apple's density solution for cramming everything to the right of the notch or Dynamic Island. But on the Mac, even in the menu bar, that kind of screen real estate pressure simply does not exist.

I have been running macOS 27 Golden Gate on my 15-inch MacBook Air since the first developer beta dropped. I have noticed my general awareness of the battery percentage has gone down, because it is simply less legible to my eyes than it used to be.

I hope Apple revisits this design decision down the road, especially if it affects more users. In the meantime, I have at least solved the problem for myself.

I built a simple menu bar utility with Codex that clearly and explicitly shows the current battery status and percentage, giving me the visual clarity I expect. If you think it might be useful to you, you can download and install it for free here.
